identity.title: MokA: Multimodal Low-Rank Adaptation for MLLMs

problem.claim: Efficiently fine-tune multimodal large language models while using both modality-specific information and cross-modal interactions.

gap.claim: The authors report that many existing efficient multimodal fine-tuning methods are borrowed from language models, neglect multimodal differences, and may underuse modalities.

contributions.claim: Proposes MokA, a multimodal-aware efficient fine-tuning strategy for MLLMs.
Uses modality-specific parameters to compress unimodal information while explicitly enhancing cross-modal interaction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MokA as a more targeted efficient-adaptation solution that explicitly combines unimodal and cross-modal adaptation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments across audio-visual-text, visual-text, and speech-text scenarios and multiple backbones, including LLaMA2, Qwen2, and Qwen2.5-VL.
The authors report consistent improvements and characterize them as indicating efficacy and versatility.
The authors report conducting ablation studies and efficiency evaluations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Identifies modality neglect as a limitation of language-model-derived efficient multimodal fine-tuning methods.
Argues that effective MLLM fine-tuning requires separate unimodal and cross-modal adaptation.
Introduces MokA, combining modality-specific compression with explicit cross-modal interaction enhancement.
Reports broad scenario and backbone coverage, consistent improvements, ablations, and efficiency evaluation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a diagnosed multimodal limitation to a method whose components separately address unimodal information and cross-modal interaction.

lessons.interpretation: This provides a traceable problem-to-mechanism framing for multimodal method descriptions.
lessons.application: For a multimodal paper, map each identified modality-specific failure mode to an explicit architectural or optimization component, then state that mapping before presenting results.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the task genuinely involves only one modality or when the proposed method has no separable mechanisms.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical results, datasets, baselines, parameter or compute budgets, or statistical details for the reported improvements.
It does not specify how unimodal compression or cross-modal enhancement is implemented, nor which ablations isolate each component.
The abstract does not provide evidence sufficient to independently verify the efficacy, versatility, or novelty claims.
